title: Frontend: Make Counter
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Make Counter. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({initial,commands}). Commands are increment, decrement, reset, or value. Apply them to one private counter, returning its value after each command. Reset restores initial.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Capture the current count and initial value inside a factory invocation.
alternativeApproaches: Add a bounded variant that reports rejected transitions without letting count and error state diverge.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Independent instances; repeated reset; negative values.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
